 Appearance:
 Shri Amit Jain - Advocate for the applicant.
 Smt. Garima Yadav - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State.

Order 
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 439 of Cr.P.C., 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.138/2025 registered at Police Station - Khimlasa, District-Sagar (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 409 and 420 of IPC.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that applicant is residing at Bhopal and preparing for competitive exams.
He was not the grain merchant and in ordinary course of nature, he was not involved in selling and purchasing of agricultural produce form the farmers.
Main allegation is against Sagarmal.
At the time of vacation, he was cooperating to the business of his uncle (Tau Ji) and this fact has also come on the record.
Hence, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

3. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that when the applicant came on leave or vacation, he was also involved NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:25461 2 MCRC-20947-2025 in purchasing the grain from the farmers.

As per the case diary, the applicant and his family members purchased grains from the farmers and has not paid Rs.22,00,000/- that is pending and on that basis offence under Sections 406, 409 and 420 of IPC is under investigation.

Hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
4.
Heard the parties and perused the case diary.

5. Looking to the facts and circumstances coupled with the fact that trial will take time to be concluded, this Court deems it appropriate to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.
